Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment summary from transcript:
  - Acute onset (same day) of shortness of breath and pleuritic right-sided back pain with hemoptysis on two occasions.
  - Felt feverish by hand; aware of palpitations; ~2 weeks of increased tiredness/reduced exercise tolerance prior to acute respiratory symptoms.
  - Known SLE on methotrexate (immunosuppressed). Remote exam did not show acute instability based on pulse and peripheral perfusion, but formal vitals (BP, SpO2, RR, measured temp) and chest auscultation were not performed.
- DDx integration (consistent with transcript):
  - Community-acquired pneumonia: aligns with acute feverish feeling, cough with hemoptysis, pleuritic pain; clinician favored chest infection and recommended face-to-face assessment and possible antibiotics (DDx likelihood: High).
  - Pulmonary embolism (± pulmonary infarct): fits acute pleuritic pain, hemoptysis and palpitations; SLE increases thrombosis risk (DDx likelihood: Moderate). No classical provoking factors reported; pulse was not markedly tachycardic on remote check and no SpO2 available.
  - SLE-related pulmonary involvement (lupus pneumonitis or diffuse alveolar hemorrhage): possible given SLE and hemoptysis, but no other systemic flare features documented and patient was not clearly hypoxic (DDx likelihood: Moderate).
- Conflict noted: Patient initially gave name as “Tracy Chapman” but later the clinician addressed the patient as “Doris” (conflict in recorded name).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- 1) Community-acquired pneumonia — High likelihood.
  - Justification: Acute onset feverish feeling, cough with hemoptysis, localized pleuritic pain and shortness of breath; attending clinician favored chest infection and recommended face-to-face auscultation and possible antibiotics.
- 2) Pulmonary embolism (with possible pulmonary infarct) — Moderate likelihood.
  - Justification: Acute pleuritic pain, hemoptysis and palpitations consistent with PE; SLE increases thrombosis risk even without classic provoking factors. No SpO2 or imaging to exclude; D‑dimer/imaging may be required based on face-to-face assessment.
- 3) SLE‑related pulmonary involvement (lupus pneumonitis or diffuse alveolar hemorrhage) — Moderate likelihood.
  - Justification: Known SLE and presentation with hemoptysis, fever and acute dyspnea can reflect autoimmune pulmonary processes; requires exclusion by imaging and laboratory tests.
